name: Marketing strategy to first-life program
description: One Marketing Room execution turns retained company evidence into one complete strategy and its executable first-life portfolio; deterministic materialization follows without another Room turn.

stages.objective: Create one complete, source-backed go-to-market strategy and its first-life operating portfolio in a single Marketing Room run. Use retained onboarding, baseline, administrator status when present, company memory, and current evidence. Load relevant Marketing skills directly and synthesize once; do not run another planning or validation conversation. Separate observed facts from professional recommendations and preserve material unknowns. Define a specific wedge, positioning, discoverable audience, offer framing, messaging pillars, alternatives, channel rationale, risks, measures with kill criteria, dependencies, and expected outcome. Design two to four evidence-backed, provider-neutral Runtime task proposals. Every first-life portfolio must include one bounded awareness-to-learning campaign experiment with motion_class market_response_experiment that tests the strategy through the strongest evidence-supported audience channel; do not prescribe a provider or account. Classify other motions as pipeline_development, evidence_decision, or other according to their business purpose. The remaining motions adapt to company evidence. Each proposal states title, bounded objective, reason, expected outcome, success measure, evidence references, dependencies, motion class, effect class, priority, and optional exact targets. Do not select a playbook, Company Room, provider, supported action, or execution mechanism. Do not pad unrelated work and perform no provider action.
Validate and materialize the accepted provider-neutral portfolio as ordered, idempotent proposed Runtime tasks.
